proposed_quote: HpmB is necessary for the extracellular secretion and activation of HpmA.
notes: DOI 10.1128/jb.172.3.1206-1216.1990 (Uphoff & Welch 1990 J Bacteriol, PMID 2407716, PMCID PMC208585) resolves; P. mirabilis 477-12 isolate, organism matches HI4320 row (strain_diff trivial). Documents secretion: abstract states HpmB necessary for extracellular secretion of HpmA; NH2-terminal seq of purified extracellular HpmA. BUT cited quote ('FhaC proved to be unable to mediate secretion...HpmB') mentions FhaC, which is the Bordetella TpsB and is NOT in this 1990 paper; quote not_found in this ref (came from a different TPS heterologous-secretion paper). Proposed verbatim secretion sentence from same ref.

DOI 10.1107/S174430911302962X (Baelen et al 2013 Acta Cryst F, PMID 24316822, PMCID PMC3855712) resolves; H. influenzae, matches Rd KW20 row. Quote 'HxuA is secreted by its specific transporter HxuB. HxuA/HxuB belongs to the so-called two-partner secretion systems (TPSs) that are characterized by a conserved N-terminal domain in the secreted protein which is essential for secretion.' is verbatim in abstract. Documents TPS (T5bSS) secretion explicitly.

DOI 10.1128/IAI.72.4.1874-1884.2004 (Ward, Mock, Hansen 2004 Infect Immun, PMID 15039306, PMCID PMC375143) resolves; H. ducreyi 35000, matches 35000HP row. Quote verbatim opening sentence of abstract. Documents secretion: detected in concentrated culture supernatant; lspB (FhaC homolog) mutant abolishes LspA1/LspA2 in supernatant; complementation restores. Strict secretion evidence present.

Same ref as T5SS_13 (DOI 10.1128/IAI.72.4.1874-1884.2004, PMID 15039306). Quote verbatim. LspA2 secretion machinery-dependent (LspB/FhaC homolog) and supernatant detection documented in abstract. T5bSS.

DOI 10.1016/j.ijmm.2013.11.021 (Pramanik et al 2014 Int J Med Microbiol, PMID 24462008) resolves; S. marcescens, matches Db11 row (species match, strain not specified in abstract). Quote 'The ShlA hemolysin of Serratia marcescens is secreted across the outer membrane by the ShlB protein; ShlB belongs to the two-partner secretion system (type Vb)' is the verbatim opening of the abstract (abstract continues '...a subfamily of the Omp85...'). Documents OM secretion via TPS/T5bSS, with secretion-impaired ShlB mutants.

DOI 10.1084/jem.20020407 (Comanducci et al 2002 J Exp Med, PMID 12045242, PMCID PMC2193550) resolves; N. meningitidis MC58 row, organism matches (paper describes NadA across hypervirulent lineages incl MC58/ET5). Quote IS verbatim in abstract. BUT under STRICT rubric the quote documents adhesin/oligomerization/epithelial-binding, NOT secretion or surface export. Abstract calls NadA a 'surface antigen' (surface localization) but performs no secretion/translocation assay; NadA T5cSS export is established elsewhere, not in this ref. Flag for human review; do not auto-replace.

DOI 10.1093/emboj/19.22.5989 (Hoiczyk et al 2000 EMBO J, PMID 11080146, PMCID PMC305836) resolves; Yersinia YadA, organism matches Y. enterocolitica 8081 row. Quote 'an N-terminal oval head domain is followed by a putative coiled-coil rod and terminated by a C-terminal membrane anchor domain.' is verbatim in abstract. BUT this is structural/domain-organization of trimeric adhesins (YadA/UspA); the paper documents adhesin structure, autoagglutination, host-cell/collagen binding, NOT a secretion or surface-export assay. No strict secretion evidence in this ref. Flag for human review.

DOI 10.1111/j.1462-2920.2010.02174.x (Salacha et al 2010 Environ Microbiol, PMID 20192961) resolves; P. aeruginosa, matches PAO1 row (PlpD Q9HYQ6 is PAO1). Quote two spans both verbatim in abstract: 'We discovered a novel secreted protein by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, PlpD' and 'The association between a TpsB component and a passenger protein is a unique hybrid organization that we propose to classify as Type Vd.' (ellipsis elides intervening text). Documents secretion: 'the patatin moiety is secreted' while C-terminus stays in OM. Defines T5dSS.

DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0047069 (Oberhettinger et al 2012 PLoS ONE, PMID 23056583, PMCID PMC3467248) resolves. Paper covers intimin/invasin of enteropathogenic Yersiniae and E. coli; row is E. coli O157:H7 Sakai eae (intimin) -> strain_diff acceptable for conserved inverse-autotransporter family (paper explicitly studies E. coli intimin). Quote two spans both verbatim: 'the N-terminal beta-barrel domain acts as a translocation pore to secrete the C-terminal passenger domain' and 'we propose that this class of autotransporters be termed Type Ve secretion.' Documents secretion/translocation (Bam- and SurA-dependent passenger export); defines T5eSS.
